title: Suffolk Career Fair: Innovation, Business Management & Sports
organizer: Suffolk University Career Equity, Development & Success
organizer_blurb: Suffolk University's career center, which runs employer events, fairs and career programming for students and alumni.
summary: A fall career fair at Sargent Hall focused on innovation, business management and sports employers. A good chance to meet recruiters on campus.
description: Career fair held in the Keches Room on the first floor of Sargent Hall, 120 Tremont Street. Employers table and students walk the room to talk with recruiters about jobs and internships. Registration runs through the Suffolk Handshake career fair listing linked from the event page. The page does not list participating employers, dress code or eligibility; check Handshake for the employer list before you go.
dates_note: Tuesday, Nov 17, 2026, 12–2 pm.
eligibility: Not stated on the event page; registration is through Suffolk's Handshake.

title: Careers in Non-Profit & Social Impact: Employer Panel and Networking
organizer: Suffolk University Career Center and Center for Community Engagement
organizer_blurb: Suffolk's career center, co-hosting with the university's community engagement office.
summary: An alumni and employer panel on nonprofit and social-impact careers, followed by networking with speakers and tabling Boston nonprofits.
description: Panel discussion with Q&A featuring alumni and nonprofit employer panelists, then open networking where students can meet the speakers and several Boston-area nonprofits that will be tabling. Held in the Stoll Room (4th floor) of the Sawyer Building, 8 Ashburton Place. Register through the Suffolk Handshake event page linked from the listing. Accommodation requests go to the Career Center before the event.
dates_note: Thursday, Nov 12, 2026, 12:15–2 pm.
eligibility: Not stated; aimed at Suffolk students, registration via Suffolk Handshake.

title: Networking Lunch and Panel Session for First-Gen Students
organizer: Suffolk University Career Equity, Development & Success
organizer_blurb: Suffolk University's career center, which runs employer events, fairs and career programming for students and alumni.
summary: A lunch for first-generation Suffolk students with alumni, employer partners and staff: elevator pitch practice, a career panel and networking.
description: Three-part session: a few students practice elevator pitches with invited guests and get feedback, a Q&A panel where guests talk through their career paths and advice, then networking over lunch. Guests include alumni, employer partners and staff. Held in Room 140 on the first floor of 73 Tremont Street (Stahl Building). Register through the Suffolk Handshake event page.
dates_note: Tuesday, Oct 27, 2026, 11 am–12:30 pm.
eligibility: For first-generation Suffolk students; register on Suffolk Handshake.

title: Peer Perspectives: Senior x First-Year Connections
organizer: Suffolk University Career Equity, Development & Success
organizer_blurb: Suffolk University's career center, which runs employer events, fairs and career programming for students and alumni.
summary: An evening networking night where first-year students meet senior student leaders and talk about academics, activities and internship searching.
description: Informal in-person meet-and-greet in the Career Center lobby at 73 Tremont Street. Senior student leaders from offices and departments across campus share what they learned about classes, extracurriculars, community engagement and landing internships. Run with the Career Center's Senior Career Ambassadors. Register through the Suffolk Handshake event page.
dates_note: Wednesday, Nov 4, 2026, 6–7:30 pm.
eligibility: Aimed at first-year Suffolk students, especially those in their first term.

title: Suffolk Career Center Employer Coffee Chats
organizer: Suffolk University Career Equity, Development & Success
organizer_blurb: Suffolk University's career center, which runs employer events, fairs and career programming for students and alumni.
summary: Drop-in coffee chats in the Career Center lobby where students meet representatives from a different employer each session.
description: Informal drop-in format: grab coffee and talk with professionals from a visiting employer about their career paths, company culture and the skills they hire for. Held in the Career Center lobby, first floor of 73 Tremont Street, usually around midday. Each chat has its own listing on the Career Center events page with a Handshake link to sign up. Fall 2026 hosts listed so far include state agencies, an insurer and nonprofit employers.
dates_note: Roughly every week or two during the semester, 12–1:30 pm; fall 2026 dates listed include Oct 20, Oct 27, Nov 10 and Dec 1.
eligibility: Students are encouraged to attend; no other requirements stated.

title: Boston Tech Week
organizer_blurb: Venture firm a16z runs Tech Week, a series of city-wide weeks where local companies and groups host their own events.
summary: A decentralized week of startup and tech events across Boston and Cambridge, with hundreds of mixers, panels, pitch events, hackathons and dinners run by local hosts.
description: a16z brought its Tech Week format to Boston for the first time in 2026. Instead of one venue, local companies, investors and community groups each host their own events during the week (panels, demo nights, hackathons, happy hours, dinners), all listed on a shared calendar at tech-week.com where you build your own schedule and RSVP per event. Many events are free; some are invite-only or require host approval. The 2026 edition ran May 26–31. No 2027 dates had been announced as of October 2026; watch the official calendar in spring.
dates_note: 2026 edition ran May 26–31, 2026. 2027 dates not yet announced.
eligibility: Varies by event; RSVP per event, and some hosts approve or invite attendees.

title: Venture Café Cambridge: Thursday Gathering
organizer_blurb: A nonprofit that runs free programming for the innovation community, hosted at the Cambridge Innovation Center.
summary: A weekly open networking evening at CIC Cambridge in Kendall Square that draws founders, investors, researchers, corporate folks and students.
description: Open gathering every Thursday evening with themed talks, office hours and plenty of unstructured networking. Each week has its own theme (recent examples: brain health and AI, country innovation nights tied to Tough Tech Week). Hosted at CIC Cambridge in Kendall Square. Sign up for each week's gathering on the Venture Café community site; you create a free profile once and register per event. A low-pressure place to meet the Boston startup scene.
location: CIC Cambridge, Kendall Square, Cambridge, MA
dates_note: Every Thursday, about 4:30–8 pm; register for each week on the community site. Upcoming dates listed through Dec 17, 2026.
eligibility: Open to everyone; the organizer welcomes all industries and backgrounds, students included. Registration per event.

title: Startup Boston Week
organizer_blurb: A nonprofit community organization whose flagship event is New England's large annual startup conference.
summary: A five-day September conference with 100+ free sessions, panels and networking events for founders, operators, investors and students.
description: Annual week-long startup conference, now in its tenth year. Days mix talks and panels across startup functions with networking events, side events and an ecosystem fair. In 2026 it ran Sept 14–18, with programming at Boston University early in the week and Downtown Crossing later in the week (earlier editions were hosted at Suffolk). Register free on the Startup Boston site; volunteers can join the event crew. Expect the next edition in September 2027; dates not yet posted.
dates_note: Annual each September; 2026 edition ran Sept 14–18. 2027 dates not yet announced.
eligibility: Open to all industries and company stages; founders, operators, investors, students and ecosystem builders.

title: Tough Tech Week 2026
organizer_blurb: A Cambridge venture firm and lab space, spun out of MIT, that backs deep-tech startups.
summary: A week of deep-tech events across Boston and Cambridge: talks, demos, networking lunches, happy hours and facility tours on climate, health, AI and advanced systems.
description: City-wide week run by The Engine with partners across Massachusetts. The Luma calendar lists dozens of separately registered events in Kendall Square, Downtown, Central Square, Fenway and the MIT Museum, plus a few virtual ones. Formats include panels, pitch and demo days, workshops, expos and socials. Cost depends on the event: many show no price, some are cheap (around $10) and the flagship summit is expensive. Pick events on the calendar and register on each one's Luma page.
dates_note: Oct 26–30, 2026; register per event on Luma.
eligibility: Varies by event; some are listed as public, others need host approval.

title: AI Tinkerers Boston Meetup
organizer_blurb: Boston chapter of a global network of hands-on AI builders that runs demo-focused meetups.
summary: Evening demo nights where local engineers, founders and researchers show working AI systems, followed by technical Q&A and networking.
description: Roughly three-hour evening meetups built around short live code demos (agents, RAG, voice, evals, infra) rather than slides or sales pitches, then networking. Demo slots are requested on each event page. Attendance is screened: you apply to attend with a profile link, and the venue may be shared after acceptance. About a dozen events a year, often on Mondays. Next listed: Oct 26, 2026, a security-themed build night.
dates_note: About monthly, typically 6–9 pm; next listed Monday, Oct 26, 2026.
eligibility: Apply to attend; the audience is screened for active AI builders, founders, researchers and engineers.

title: Building Agents with Vercel & Jellyfish
organizer: Mass Technology Leadership Council (MTLC) with Vercel, Jellyfish, MAIC and Pillar VC
organizer_blurb: Massachusetts' tech industry association, which lists member and partner events across the region.
summary: A technical evening on building production AI agents with a live demo, hands-on build time, show-and-tell and networking.
description: Doors open with food, drinks and networking, then a live demo and conversation on agent architecture (tools, memory, orchestration, deployment) using a new agent framework from Vercel, audience Q&A, about half an hour to build an agent solo or in groups, and quick three-minute show-and-tells before more networking. Hosted at Pillar VC on Boylston Street. Registration through the Luma link on the MTLC listing. MTLC's events page lists other member and virtual events throughout the year.
dates_note: Thursday, Oct 22, 2026, 5:30–8 pm.
eligibility: Not stated; listed as a member event, register via Luma.

title: Startup Grind Boston Events
organizer_blurb: Boston chapter of the global Startup Grind founder community.
summary: Fireside chats, pitch nights, founder showcases and workshops for the Boston startup community.
description: Chapter events range from fireside chats with founders and investors to pitch battles, founder showcases and tactical workshops on fundraising and growth, plus free virtual pitch-practice sessions. Fall 2026 listings include an AI founder demo showcase (Oct 22), an investor-readiness session tied to TechCrunch Founder Summit (Nov 3) and a startup pitch night (Nov 18). RSVP on each event page; prices are not listed for most events.
dates_note: Several events a month, no fixed schedule; upcoming listed Oct 22, Nov 3 and Nov 18, 2026.
eligibility: Not stated; RSVP per event.

title: Boston Python User Group
organizer_blurb: One of the largest local Python user groups in the world, welcoming all skill levels.
summary: Monthly presentation nights and project nights, plus casual Python Over Coffee meetups, for Python users of every level.
description: Presentation nights feature an hour or so of talks, often with short lightning talks. Project nights are informal: bring your own project, get help or help others. Python Over Coffee is a casual weekend meetup in Arlington. Events are mostly around Boston and Cambridge and are often hosted by sponsor companies. RSVP on Meetup; the group also has a Slack workspace and allows job posts that follow its rules.
dates_note: Presentation and project nights monthly; Python Over Coffee most Sundays 12:30 pm in Arlington.
eligibility: Open to all skill levels; RSVP on Meetup.

title: Boston Python Online Office Hours
organizer_blurb: One of the largest local Python user groups in the world, welcoming all skill levels.
summary: Unstructured lunchtime Zoom drop-ins where you can ask Python questions and meet other members of the Boston Python community.
description: Casual online office hours on Zoom at noon Eastern every other Monday. No agenda: drop in with a question, a bug or just to chat with other Python users. RSVP on the Boston Python Meetup page to get the link. An easy way to join the community without traveling to an in-person event.
dates_note: Every other Monday at 12 pm ET; next listed Oct 26, 2026.
eligibility: Open to all; RSVP on Meetup.

title: Boston New Technology: Precision Pitch Practice
organizer_blurb: A Boston startup community that has run showcases and founder networking for more than 15 years.
summary: A weekly online session where founders pitch and get feedback; listeners are welcome, co-hosted with Startup Grind Boston.
description: Low-pressure Zoom session at noon on Thursdays: founders deliver pitches and get structured feedback from the group, and anyone can join to listen and learn. BNT also runs Deck Doctors on some Tuesdays, a hands-on review of real pitch decks covering story, value proposition and traction. Sign up for each session on Luma (linked from Meetup) to receive that week's Zoom link.
dates_note: Every Thursday at 12 pm ET; upcoming listed Oct 22, Oct 29 and Nov 5.
eligibility: Open; founders pitch and listeners are welcome. Sign up per session.

title: Cross University Innovators Mixer: AI Is Changing Entry-Level Jobs. So WTF Should Students Learn?
organizer_blurb: Startup Boston is a nonprofit that runs events and programs for founders, students and the Boston startup community.
summary: A student-focused panel and mixer at Klaviyo's downtown office about how AI is changing entry-level tech jobs. It is a short walk from Suffolk and built for undergrads and grad students.
description: Startup Boston's Cross University Innovators Mixer series is listed on its events directory for November 5, 2026. This edition is a panel of students from regional colleges and startup and tech leaders, followed by food and networking. Topics include which entry-level tasks AI is changing, the technical and human skills employers want, and what makes recent grads stand out. An optional tour of Klaviyo's office is offered. The previous mixer drew students from 54 schools. Student tickets require host approval, and attendees should bring a photo ID for building security. Price and start time are not posted on the Luma page.
location: Klaviyo, 125 Summer St, Floor 7, Boston, MA
dates_note: Thursday, November 5, 2026 per the Startup Boston events directory; time not shown on the Luma page.
eligibility: Undergraduate or graduate students (Student Ticket) and university program leaders (Educator Ticket); registration subject to host approval. Students need not be AI experts or CS majors.

title: Built in Boston: A Student Founder Pitch Showcase
organizer: Startup Boston with the City of Boston
organizer_blurb: Startup Boston is a nonprofit that runs events and programs for founders, students and the Boston startup community.
summary: Student-founded Boston startups pitch at City Hall for cash prizes, with a free audience. Good for meeting student founders, judges and city startup staff, or for pitching your own company.
description: A live pitch showcase at Boston City Hall. Selected student teams get 5 minutes to pitch and 3 minutes of judge Q&A, with prizes of $1,000, $750 and $500. Pitching teams need at least one current-student founder, a company incorporated and headquartered in Boston proper, a separate business bank account, and a software or hardware component. Teams apply through an Airtable form linked on the Luma page. Judges are to be announced. Attendance is free with registration.
location: Boston City Hall, 1 City Hall Square, Boston, MA
dates_note: Wednesday, November 18, 2026, 5:30 pm (per foundercal listing). Pitch application deadline not posted.
eligibility: Audience: registration required, no restrictions stated. Pitching teams: at least one current student founder; company incorporated and headquartered in Boston proper.

title: FounderConnect: Startup Resources & Networking Expo
organizer_blurb: Startup Boston is a nonprofit that runs events and programs for founders, students and the Boston startup community.
summary: A free evening expo at CIC Cambridge where founders meet legal, financial, marketing and technical service providers one on one. Useful for student founders and anyone building a side project into a company.
description: An in-person networking expo on the 5th floor (Venture Cafe) of 1 Broadway in Cambridge, run by Startup Boston with CIC's Social Impact Cohort. The format is 1:1 conversations with service providers across legal, financial, marketing and technical fields. The listing says it is for startup founders and cofounders at any stage. Registration is on Luma. Attendance numbers are not posted.
dates_note: Tuesday, November 17, 2026, 5:30 pm (per foundercal listing).
eligibility: Not stated on the page; described as for startup founders and cofounders at any stage.

title: MIT Energy & Climate Night 2026

summary: A free, public evening of about 50 poster-style demos from MIT labs, student teams and climate startups. A good place to talk directly with researchers and early-stage founders.

title: NYC Physical AI Workshop and Meetup (Voxel51 x Nebius)
organizer_blurb: Voxel51 makes FiftyOne, an open-source toolkit for computer vision datasets; Nebius is an AI cloud provider.

Networking closes the event. Anyone can join the networking; the workshop requires a company, university or government email, not Gmail or Yahoo. No price is listed. Space is limited.

dates_note: Saturday, November 14, 2026, 1:30–4:30 pm ET.
eligibility: Networking open to anyone; workshop requires a company, university (.edu) or government email and a laptop.

title: NYC Code and Coffee 89 at Datadog HQ
organizer: New York Code & Coffee (hosted by Datadog)
organizer_blurb: New York Code & Coffee is a volunteer-run co-working meetup for developers of all levels.
summary: A relaxed Sunday co-working session inside Datadog's Manhattan HQ where developers of every level code and talk. Easy, low-pressure way to meet NYC engineers.

eligibility: Open to all skill levels (as stated).
